stories.title: No Criminal Charges for Driver of Truck That Plowed Into Crowd in Kansas
stories.summary: A district attorney called the crash a tragedy but said that it did not meet the criteria for criminal prosecution. After a weekslong investigation into a driver whose truck plowed into a crowd on a soccer field in Kansas, killing two people and injuring 10 others, a prosecutor has announced that no criminal charges would be filed. The events on Oct. 17 were a tragedy and a mistake, the district attorney said, but the evidence was insufficient to prove that the driver had intended to hurt anyone. “Not everybody may be at peace with this decision,” Marc Bennett, the district attorney of Sedgwick County, said at a news conference on Thursday.

stories.summary: By pleading guilty to accessory to murder after the fact, Richard Glossip will avoid a retrial of the first-degree murder charge. Richard Glossip, who spent nearly 30 years on death row in Oklahoma before receiving a stay of execution from the U.S. Supreme Court, pleaded guilty to a lesser charge on Thursday in order to avoid a new murder trial. Mr. Glossip, 63, pleaded guilty to accessory to murder after the fact, his lawyer, Don Knight, said in a statement. The plea agreement means that Mr. Glossip will not be retried on a first-degree murder charge.

The recovery took nearly a full day while engineers gradually restored services, highlighting how embedded the tech giant's services are in modern society.
